Great! To start, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child (or children) you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The name(s) of the child/children
- Their age(s) or date(s) of birth

This will help me determine which path of the eligibility assessment applies to your situation. Child Benefit has different rules depending on whether children are:
- **Under 16** (generally automatic eligibility if other conditions are met)
- **16-19** (must be in approved education or training, or on certain extensions)
- **20 or over** (not eligible for Child Benefit)

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Result: INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry, but you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**The Rule:**
Child Benefit can only be claimed for:
- Children under 16, OR
- Young people aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training

**Your Situation:**
Since Alex is 21 years old, he no longer qualifies as a child under the Child Benefit rules, even though he lives at home with you.

**What This Means:**
- Your entitlement to Child Benefit for Alex ended when he turned 20 (or when he left approved education/training if that was before then)
- Simply living at home doesn't extend eligibility beyond the age limits

**If You Have Other Children:**
If you have any other children under 20 who are in approved education or training, I'd be happy to check their eligibility for you. Just let me know their names and ages!

Is there anything else I can help you with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. 

Actually, I should mention - Alex does receive Universal Credit in his own name because he's been struggling to find work. Does that make any difference to whether I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that additional information. I understand that can be a difficult situation.

Unfortunately, **no, it doesn't make a difference**. The fact that Alex receives Universal Credit in his own name doesn't change the Child Benefit eligibility rules.

**Why:**
Child Benefit eligibility is based on the child's age and their education/training status - not on their income or benefit entitlements. The rules are:
- Children must be under 16, OR
- Aged 16-19 and in approved full-time education or training

Since Alex is 21 years old, he falls outside these age limits regardless of what other benefits he may be receiving.

**Universal Credit vs Child Benefit:**
These are separate benefits with different eligibility criteria:
- Universal Credit is assessed based on income, savings, and work-seeking status
- Child Benefit is based on age and education/training status

So while Alex can continue to claim Universal Credit if he meets those criteria, that won't make him eligible for Child Benefit.

**Is there anything else I can help with?**
- Do you have any other children under 20 that you'd like me to check eligibility for?
- Do you need any information about other support that might be available to Alex?
